newsitem.title: USA: W.R. Grace sees Q4 charges, EPS mid-$0.60.
newsitem.headline: W.R. Grace sees Q4 charges, EPS mid-$0.60.

text.p: W.R. Grace & Co said Thursday that it expects fourth quarter operating earnings per share to be in the mid-$0.60 range, including operating losses from the divestment of its air emissions control business.

The TEC Systems emissions business is to be divested in 1997, and the estimate includes losses from that business in the fourth quarter and the accrual of that business's 1997 losses, said company spokeswoman Mary Lou Kromer.

Kromer said the estimate does not includes special charges the company expects to record in the fourth quarter for several matters, including asbestos bodily injury litigation and claims, restructuring activities and asset impairments.
Wall Street had expected fourth quarter earnings of $0.83 per share for the company and full-year earnings of $2.40 per share, according to First Call consensus estimates.

Excluding special charges such as TEC losses, W.R. Grace said operating earnings will be around $0.75 to $0.79 a share, compared to earnings from continuing operations of $0.63 a share in the 1995 quarter.
The company said its 1996 full-year earnings per share before special items would be about 15 percent higher than 1995 operating earnings of $2.03 a share.
Kromer said the company has not estimated net earnings because it does not know the amount of special charges to be taken for the year.
Grace said sales and earnings growth in the fourth quarter will be less than expected because of continued weakness in some of its packaging and catalyst markets.
The supplier of packaging materials and specialty chemicals said in October that it would divest four non-core businesses, including TEC.
Grace said today it had been in discussions with a potential buyer for TEC but that those discussions had ended.
Divestiture of the other three businesses remains on schedule, it said.

Besides a previously announced pact to sell its Amicon business for $125 million, the competitive bidding process to sell its cocoa and specialty polymers businesses is in the final stages, Grace said.
It said it expects to name buyers for those businesses by early 1997.
